correctness.rationale: For all integers m≥2 and B>0, a feasible Euclidean embedding has squared allowed-edge lengths 1 apart from the spine length s²≤1 and centered variance D_m. Rayleigh gives λ₂≤B/D_m for arbitrary, including asymmetric, conductances. Explicit nonnegative rational weights of sum D_m attain λ₂=1: page-standard multiplicity m−1 and an independent axial eigenvector give eigenvalue one; the two remaining nonzero eigenvalues have real roots with shifted product P_m>0 and sum S_m>2, hence are both >1. Scaling attains the bound, and the strict spine slack when m≥5 forces spine weight zero for every optimizer. Two symbolic all-m characteristic and budget identity suites plus 119 independent finite full-Laplacian assemblies passed. The m=1 and altered edge-cost regimes are not proved.

value.rationale: A natural finite spectral network design problem yields an exact, nontrivial structural phase boundary: an allowed common edge is strictly used by constructed optima below five pages but necessarily has zero conductance in every optimum from five pages onward. Closed-form rational optimum, explicit positive remaining allocations and an all-competitor Euclidean bound make the result useful as a design rule and an exact spectral optimization benchmark, not merely a routine reformulation.
